doc: Self-validation manifest — the loop must never merge a capability it cannot itself VALIDATE in CI. Each active capability declares HOW it is proven keyless (an e2e spec the CI e2e job runs, or a unit/degrade test the `verify` job runs). A capability whose validation needs an env the loop can't supply (an OWNER SECRET) sets requiresOwnerSecret + ownerActionId; until the owner wires the secret in CI, the self-validation tripwire (scripts/check-self-validation.mjs) goes RED and the PR can't merge. SURFACING (an unmet capability must be visible to the owner in BOTH channels, else it's a bug): an urgent OWNER_ACTION 'validation-capability-<service>' (priority: urgent, blocks: validation) in PENDING_OPS.md AND the validation.unmet list in LOOP_HEALTH.md (refresh from `check-self-validation.mjs --readiness`). Non-secret CI envs a check needs (e.g. EMAIL_CAPTURE_DIR — a temp dir) go in requiresCiEnv so a missing one BLOCKS instead of silently skipping. HONESTY (readiness auditors reconcile this, maker!=checker): a declared spec/test must genuinely EXERCISE the capability — a 'validated' capability that is really an un-exercised critical path behind a stub/mock is an artifact-integrity FAIL (the email-verification trap). status: active|planned|retired. Extend this as the app grows; the auditor + factory keep it in sync.

capabilities.summary: Signup → working dashboard (never an error screen), core navigation, pantry/cook surfaces — the outcome-asserting BUILDS!=WORKS suite.
Waitlist double-opt-in email SIDE-EFFECT integrity — submit → a real confirmation email is dispatched → retrieve it from the capture sink → follow the confirm link → confirmed (no fake success).

Server-side subscription entitlement gating + tier resolution (premium / annual / family), incl. the RevenueCat webhook event→entitlement classification (grant/revoke/ignore) and product-id→tier mapping, fail-open when the flag is off — validated keyless via unit tests (no live Stripe/RevenueCat key needed for the entitlement logic).
The TEST-ONLY rate-limit bypass (RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED) FAILS CLOSED in a production runtime — proves abuse protection can never be silently disabled live.
The email capture sink (EMAIL_CAPTURE_DIR) FAILS CLOSED in a production runtime and the provider transport fails open with a warning when unconfigured — keyless unit-validated.

The public no-account receipt demo (§34) enforces a per-IP AND global per-instance daily spend ceiling (checkDemoQuota) plus a per-IP rate limit, so an anonymous / IP-rotating caller cannot drain the LLM budget on a given instance (the global counter backstops IP spoofing). NOTE: the counter is in-memory per Node instance — a TRUE cross-instance global cap needs the Redis backing tracked in PENDING_OPS (llm-quota-redis-upgrade); pre-launch traffic is owner-gated so the per-instance bound suffices until then. The route also degrades to a calm 503 JSON (never a crash / fake success) when no Gemini key is configured. Validated keyless: the ceiling logic by unit test, the route's degrade + POST-only behaviour by the e2e smoke spec.

The gated-beta invite funnel (§34 Part B): a waitlisted person redeems the code the owner issued them at /join → POST /api/invite/redeem validates the code and, on success, grants the pre-launch site-gate cookie so /signup is reachable (the full app stays gated otherwise). Hardened like the other public surface: per-IP rate limit, bounded input, keyless normalize+format validation BEFORE any DB work, idempotent redeem (a code is a per-person beta KEY — a cleared cookie / second device re-redeems safely), and generic non-enumerating error messages (invalid / malformed / not-found all read the same). Validated keyless: the code alphabet/shape/normalization/generation by unit test (no key needed), and the route's reachability + generic-reject + POST-only behaviour by the e2e journeys spec (CI runs with the gate OFF, so a made-up code exercises the real validate+lookup+reject path).

The GTM §11 media-gen adapter (@gm/core/media): produces multi-format marketing creative (IMAGE via Nano Banana / VIDEO via Gemini Omni Flash / MUSIC via Lyria 3 / VOICEOVER via Gemini TTS) on the EXISTING Gemini key — no separate media-gen key to connect; publishing stays gated (Track H / §13), the adapter only STAGES + audits. Best-effort + degrade-by-default like every LLM call: AUDIT-FIRST (the deterministic maker!=checker not-obviously-AI + FTC-disclosure gate runs BEFORE any paid call, so a slop/undisclosed request is 'rejected' spending nothing), then DEGRADE (no Gemini/Vertex credential -> 'unavailable' without touching the network; any API failure/timeout -> 'error') so a media call can never block or crash the marketing loop. Preview model ids are pinned in one place (MEDIA_MODELS) and every call is wall-clock bounded. Validated keyless: the pre-publish audit gate (FTC disclosure presence + slop-vocabulary denylist), the adapter's audit-first + no-key degrade + model-id pinning behaviour, AND — via an injected fake provider — the real success mapping (image bytes / video operation name / inline audio -> ok asset) plus the throw/empty/timeout -> error degrade paths, all by unit test (a billed key is only needed to hit the live preview models, which are owner-gated; every branch of the adapter's own logic is exercised keyless). The batch STAGING consumer (stageCreative) sits on top of the adapter: it turns a CreativeBrief (the set of creative one launch beat needs) into a reviewable metadata-only StagingManifest plus the raw assets for the Track-H/§13 approval gate, degrade-by-default and never-throw like the adapter (one bad item is recorded, never aborts the batch); its orchestration, per-format dispatch, audit-first rejection, no-key degrade, provider-error, and manifest tally are all exercised keyless via an injected fake provider (staging.test.ts). The AUTHORING half is the launch-briefs consumer (launch-briefs.ts): LAUNCH_CREATIVE_BRIEFS hand-authors the real CreativeBriefs each launch beat needs (grounded in docs/brand/LAUNCH_PLAN.md + BRAND_KIT.md), auditLaunchBriefs proves every authored item is audit-clean (disclosure present + no slop vocabulary), and stageLaunchCreative drives the whole set through stageCreative — the batch invocation site the launch plan needs. Validated keyless (launch-briefs.test.ts): well-formed unique briefs, every item audit-clean, no-key all-'unavailable' degrade, and — via the injected fake provider — every item stages 'ok'. Producing real assets + persisting them on a schedule remains the owner-gated edge (a billed Gemini preview key + Track-H storage/channel).
